quiz_1.text: In "The cat quickly climbed the tree", which word is an adverb?
Which sentence means the same as "Nobody except Sam passed the test"?
options: Sam was the only one who failed.

mini_lesson: An apostrophe can show that something belongs to someone. This is called possession. In "the dog's bone", the apostrophe tells us the bone belongs to the dog.
Rule: one owner means add 's, as in the girl's bag. Many owners ending in s means add ' after the s, as in the girls' bags. Its with no apostrophe shows ownership. It's is short for it is.

Example: one boy owns a bike, so it is the boy's bike. Three boys own a football, so it is the boys' football. A dog and its tail: "The dog wagged its tail." There is no apostrophe, because its shows ownership.

To check, ask who owns it and how many owners there are. One owner: apostrophe before the s. Many owners ending in s: apostrophe after the s. For its, try saying it is. If that does not fit, leave the apostrophe out.

The wolves howls woke the villagers, and it's said that the pack's leader was huge.
The wolves' howls woke the villager's, and it's said that the pack's leader was huge.
The wolves' howls woke the villagers, and it's said that the pack's leader was huge.
The wolves' howls woke the villagers, and its said that the pack's leader was huge.
hints: Check one apostrophe at a time. Start with 'howls'. Do the howls belong to the wolves?
A plural noun that already ends in s takes the apostrophe after the s. An apostrophe never turns a single word into a plain plural.
Check each apostrophe in turn. Ask whether the word owns something, or whether it is short for 'it is'. A plain plural needs no apostrophe.
